extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent agents, and legal practitioners seeking comparative international patent law guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the substantive legal standards and procedural requirements for obtaining, maintaining, and enforcing patents across multiple national jurisdictions as described in a patentees' manual. Covers patentability, term, fees, working requirements, assignment, revocation, and enforcement rules country-by-country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for infringement and aggravated circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringers are liable to damages; penalties may be imposed for the benefit of the Treasury. Where the infringer has been a workman of the patentee, or is associated with such workman, the circumstances are considered to be aggravated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both civil recovery of damages and penal penalties; severity increased where the infringer is a workman or associated with the patentee's workman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for falsely claiming to be a patentee or improper advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties are imposed on persons who wrongfully state themselves to be patentees, or continue to call themselves patentees after the lapse of the patent, and on patentees advertising as such without indicating the special object for which the patents have been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising/claims must not mislead about patent status; failure may attract fines or other penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Granting procedure (administrative referral and ministerial grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor may submit his invention to the Home Minister, who will refer the application to Commissioners for examination, and if their report be favourable the Minister will grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent grant depends on ministerial action informed by Commissioner reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Patent term, fees and secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a patent cannot exceed ten years (fixed by the Government). The patentee must pay specified sums into the Treasury and for the seal. The specification is kept secret until the expiration of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms are capped; payment and secrecy rules apply during the patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Extension of patent term procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be extended when the importance of the invention justifies it, but application must be made therefor six months before the expiration of the first term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension is discretionary and requires timely application (six months before expiry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Working requirement and forfeiture for non-working or inferior products
rubrics_metrics.description: A period exclusive of the term of the patent is allowed for erection of machinery, etc., for working the patent, but should the inventor fail to carry out the same within that period, or discontinue the working for more than a year, or produce articles inferior to the original sample, the patent becomes void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent validity conditioned on timely and continuous exploitation and fidelity to sample quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Importation does not invalidate patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles made according to the invention can be imported from abroad without invalidating the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importation of foreign-made articles does not defeat the domestic patent right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chile — Assignment and enforcement (noting transfers and remedies against infringers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be assigned; transfers must be noted in the transfer book. Infringers of a patented article are liable to a fine and to the forfeiture of the article produced, and the establishment and implements used in its manufacture. Any person not being the true inventor fraudulently obtaining a patent is liable to fine or imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments must be recorded; civil and penal remedies available; fraud in procurement of patents penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colombia — Eligible applicants and subject-matter scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be obtained by the inventor, importer, or holder of a foreign patent for any invention or improvement of mechanical apparatus, combination of materials or process, and for making and sale of any manufacture or industrial product, but not for the importation of foreign productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who can apply and the kinds of inventions eligible (mechanical/apparatus/process/manufacture), excluding mere importation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colombia — Patent term limits and foreign-patent dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration of a patent cannot exceed twenty nor be less than five years, and in the case of an invention previously patented abroad such duration is subject to the earlier expiration of the prior foreign patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National term bounded between 5 and 20 years; prior foreign patents can limit domestic term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colombia — Application formalities and grant without prior examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must present a petition to the executive setting forth the nature of his invention and the number of years desired; if favourable he must furnish within forty days a full description, accompanied by drawings or models if necessary. A patent will then be issued without any previous examination as to the novelty or utility of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant is essentially administrative and at the applicant's risk — no substantive novelty/utility examination prior to grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colombia — Grounds for refusal/revocation and working requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is refused when the invention endangers public salubrity or security, or encroaches upon proprietary rights already acquired, and may be revoked if it violates existing rights. A patent becomes void if during a whole year the invention is not worked, unless due to unavoidable circumstances; importation from abroad does not invalidate the patent. Descriptions are published only on expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public safety and existing rights are exclusionary; there is an express working requirement and deferred publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congo Free State — Broad patentability and grant without examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Every discovery and improvement capable of being worked as an object of industry or commerce is patentable. Patents of invention, importation, and improvement are granted without previous examination at the risk of the applicants and without guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very broad subject-matter test (industrial applicability); administrative grant without substantive pre-grant examination — risk on applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congo Free State — Terms, fees and assignment notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents of inventions are granted for twenty years; patents of importation are limited to the term of the foreign patent; patents for improvements expire with the original patent. Government fee for each patent is 100 francs; patentees may prosecute and recover damages and obtain confiscation. Patents may be assigned and notice of the assignment must be given to the Department for Foreign Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term distinctions by patent type; fixed upfront fee; assignment notification requirement to a government department; enforcement remedies described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congo Free State — Application signatures and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents must be signed by the applicant or his attorney, and the application must be accompanied by a specification and by drawings, models, or specimens of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal signature requirement and supporting disclosure materials are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denmark — Patentability, dating and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All inventions or improvements are patentable. The patent dates from the day of the signature of the King to the patent. The term of patents of invention is fixed by the Government, and cannot exceed fifteen years; patents are granted to foreigners for five years only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal signature as date marker; government-fixed term with special shorter term for foreigners; explicit universal patentability subject to term limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denmark — Fees and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A uniform tax of 34 kroner is required for each application for a patent. A slight examination of the invention is made before granting the patent. Prolongations are not usually granted beyond the term fixed by Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modest official fee; some substantive checking; extensions uncommon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecuador (general) — Non-publication and working requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are not published, and information respecting them cannot be obtained without the tion of the Ministry of the Interior. The working of the invention must be proceeded with during the first year of the patent, and continued without intermission during the whole term. The patent does not prevent the introduction into the country of similar products manufactured abroad. Assignments of patents are not authorised; they may, however, be accomplished by the joint demand of the proprietor and of the assignee for a new patent in the name of the latter. The patent becomes void if the invention is not new, or if it has not been worked within the given time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-publication regime; strict working requirement; importation tolerated; assignments limited and require re-patenting under assignee's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecuador (law Oct 18,1880) — Terms and investment-based privileges for importers
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions protected for not less than ten or more than fifteen years. Importers of machinery or new methods not previously known in the republic are entitled to exclusive privileges: if establishment requires outlay of 25,000 dollars protection granted for 3 years, if 50,000 for 6 years, if 100,000 or more for 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiered protection for importers tied to investment thresholds; explicit minimum and maximum term ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecuador — Application, examination commission, and publication on expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must petition the executive power, explaining the invention, deliver a specimen of the manufacture, and a specification; Government appoints a Commission of three persons to examine and report to the Minister of the Interior, who presents the papers to Congress for grant or refusal. All assignments must be made by public instruments. On expiration the petition, description, and other papers are to be published and deposited in the public library of the capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-stage review involving executive, Commission and Congress; formal assignment instruments; deferred post-expiry publication and public deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecuador — Grounds for lapsing of privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Privilege lapses when the invention is declared contrary to the laws of the state, to public safety, or to police regulations; also if the inventor is convicted of having omitted from his description the true method of carrying his invention into practice, or of using secret methods not detailed in his description, or if the invention has been described and published in the press, or if the invention is not put into complete practice within a year and a day from the grant, or if the obligations of the patent are not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive grounds for forfeiture cover public-order, fraud/omission in disclosure, prior publication, and non-working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finland — Patentable subject-matter exclusions and true-inventor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for inventions or improvements in arts and manufactures. Medicines and inventions contrary to morals or public safety are not patentable. Patents are granted only to the true inventor, whether native or foreigner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral/public-safety exclusions and an explicit requirement that the applicant be the true inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finland — Patentee rights
rubrics_metrics.description: While ownership is not contested, the person to whom the privilege is granted has rights: (1) absolute property in the invention for the time specified; (2) to use the invention himself, and to sell its results to the public, or to transfer the patent to another person; (3) to prosecute persons infringing the patent in the courts of law, and to recover an indemnity for the loss sustained by the infringement; (4) to treat as an infringement the making of articles in a similar manner with unessential differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the principal exclusive rights and enforcement entitlement of the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finland — Disclosure requirements in application
rubrics_metrics.description: The person applying for a patent must deliver to the Government an exact description of his invention, with all essential details and the mode of carrying it into effect, and also the necessary plans and drawings, and models, if deemed necessary, not keeping back anything requisite to be known. The inventor must also state in what respects his invention is new, or whether it is an improvement upon an invention already used; the novelty of the invention or improvement must be specified in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires full and honest disclosure including how to carry the invention into effect; novelty must be specifically identified in claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finland — Substantive examination, term, fees, publication and working proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications are subject to an investigation into the novelty and merits. Patents are granted for terms from three to twelve years; duration fixed by Government according to industry. Government tax is 20 Finnish marks per year plus additional charges. The patentee is bound within two months from date of issue to publish the specification in two Finnish newspapers (Swedish and Finnish). The time prescribed for working is generally two years (modifiable between one and four by application). After this, proof of the working must be given every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive examination; term determined by government and tied to industry sector; ongoing working proof and mandatory local-language publication soon after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finland — Annulment grounds (non-disclosure, non-working, prior use/publication, public safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent will be annulled if the patentee has not published the specification, or proved the working within the time prescribed; if it is proved by verdict that the same invention was already in use in Finland or elsewhere, or patented by another person before application; or if it should turn out that the patent is contrary to morals or public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annulment covers failures in disclosure and working as well as prior art and public-order grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Excluded subject-matter and duration/payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The following cannot be patented: (1) Pharmaceutical compounds, or medicines of any kind; (2) schemes and projects of credit and finance. The duration of patents is fifteen years; the payment in respect of a patent for fifteen years is 1,500 francs (payable by yearly instalments of 100 francs), and the patent will expire if default is made in payment of any one instalment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain fields excluded (medicines subject to special rules); long-term fee schedule with expiration on non-payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Application formalities, language and single-object restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons desirous of obtaining a patent must apply by petition to the Minister and give a description, accompanied by drawings when needful. The petition must be in the French language, and must be restricted to a single principal object, with necessary details and proposed applications; it must mention the duration desired and give a title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict formal requirements including language, single-claimlike principal object, and specifications for title and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Grant without prior examination and absence of government guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents applied for in due form are delivered without previous examination, at the risk of the applicants, and without Government guarantee, as to the reality, the novelty, or fidelity or accuracy of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative grant system places risk of invalidity on the applicant; government offers no substantive pre-grant assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Nullity grounds (six enumerated grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are null and of no effect in the following cases: (1) not new; (2) not patentable; (3) theoretical/scientific conceptions whose industrial applications are not shown; (4) contrary to order, safety, morals, or laws of France; (5) if the title fraudulently indicates something not the true subject-matter; (6) if the description is insufficient for carrying the invention into effect or does not completely and fairly state the real methods adopted by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive statutory grounds for nullity include novelty, sufficiency of disclosure, subject-matter eligibility, and fraud in title.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Deprivation of rights for non-payment or non-working; penalties for false patentee claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee will be deprived of rights if he fails to pay the annual payment before commencement of each year; if he does not put the invention into execution in France within two years from signature; or if he ceases for two consecutive years to work the patent (unless justifying). Whoever assumes title of patentee without possessing a patent, or refers to his patent without adding 'sans garantie du gouvernement' is liable to a penalty of from 50 to 1,000 francs (doubled on repetition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining patent requires timely payments and local working; public misrepresentation of patent status is penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: France — Certificates of addition, preference period and assignment formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may make alterations/additions and obtain certificates of addition (which expire with original patent). Only the patentee and those claiming under him can, during a year, obtain a valid patent for an alteration/improvement; others may deposit an application under seal which is opened at the year's end. Assignment of whole or part must be by notarial act and after payment of instalments; assignment not valid against third parties until registered. Simple licence need not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special regime for follow-on improvements including one-year priority for original patentee; formalities and registration required for assignments to affect third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Patentability, exclusions and novelty standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for new inventions which admit of industrial use, with exceptions: inventions incompatible with laws or public morals; and inventions relating to food, medicines, and substances produced by chemical process, so far as the invention does not relate to the method of producing such articles. An invention is not regarded as new if it has already been described in a printed publication in any country, or publicly used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial applicability required; explicit exclusions; printed/public use destroys novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — First applicant rule and protection against misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: The first applicant for a patent of invention is entitled to the grant. The claim of the petitioner is void if essential contents of his application have, without permission, been taken from the descriptions, drawings, models, implements, or arrangements of another person, or from a method of manufacture used by another, and that person raises opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to first applicant combined with protection against appropriating another's confidential materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Prior user and limits of patent effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent has no effect against a person who, at the time the patentee made his application, had already been using the invention in Germany, or had made the necessary preparations for using the same; neither has it any effect in so far as the invention is intended to be used for the army or navy or in the interest of public welfare (compensation may be due). The patent does not affect means of conveyance coming temporarily within the empire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior local use and certain public-interest uses limit the patent's reach; compensation regime for public-interest limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Term, fees, expiry and revocation for non-use or non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for fifteen years, commencing with the day following the day of application. Fee of 30 marks on issue and further fees each subsequent year. The patent expires if patentee resigns or fails to pay fees within three months after due. Patents are to be annulled if invention not patentable or if essential contents were taken from another. Patent can be revoked after three years if patentee fails to carry out his invention in Germany to a suitable extent or refuses to grant licence in public-welfare interest upon adequate compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual maintenance fees with narrow grace period; revocation/compulsory licensing for lack of working or public interest refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Application formalities, provisional protection and adversarial procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be in writing and must point out in a precise manner the subject-matter to be patented, and be accompanied by drawings/models/samples where necessary; fee 20 marks on filing. When the invention is approved by the Patent Office the subject-matter will be provisionally protected and notification published. Eight weeks after publication the Patent Office must decide as to granting; objections may be lodged in writing with arguments; Office may summon parties, appoint technical examiners, and institute inquiries. Decisions are appealable within stated times; fee on appeal 20 marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure includes provisional protection, public notification, a window for objections and technical inquiries, and appeal rights — with specified fees and language requirement (German).

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Language requirement and limitation period for infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: No action will be taken upon applications which are not written in the German language. The time within which an action may be brought for an infringement of patent right is limited to three years with regard to any single case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict language mandate for filings; statutory limitation on infringement suits (three years per cause of action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Germany — Register, publication and Patent Office competence
rubrics_metrics.description: A register is kept at the Patent Office recording subject-matter, duration, names, addresses, commencements, termination, annulment, revocation; entries are published in the Reichsanzeiger. Essential parts of specifications and drawings (as permitted) will be published in an official paper. Granting, annulment, and revocation are vested in the Patent Office (Berlin) and decisions are subject to appeal. The Office must give opinion to law courts when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central administrative control with registry and publication duties; appeals and judicial interaction provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guatemala — Eligibility, application and working/quality forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted for terms of from ten to fifteen years to natives or domiciled foreigners or persons who have applied in other countries of the International Convention. Application must be made to the Ministry of the Interior explaining the invention and soliciting privilege; upon grant an exact drawing or detailed description and specimen must be furnished. Patents will be void when issued prejudicially to third-party rights, when the invention is not put into practice within a year from the date of the grant, or when abandoned for more than a year, or when the products are inferior to the specimens lodged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines eligibility under national/Convention criteria, formal disclosure requirements, and strict working and conformity requirements tied to lodged specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guatemala — Right to improve and importation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person has the right of improving the invention, but not of using the original invention, and the original inventor cannot use the improvements made by another except by agreement. Articles made abroad according to the invention can be imported without rendering the patent invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvement rights separated from original use-rights; importation permitted without invalidating the domestic patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guatemala — Annual tax payable in advance and grants for public utility
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax is reserved by the patent of from five to fifty dollars for each year of the grant, payable in advance. The same law also provides for making grants in favour of undertakings of public utility or establishment of new industries or improvements upon those already existing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees required and special grants may be made to promote public-utility undertakings or industrial establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hawaii — Application materials, examination and caveat priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An Act of August 29, 1884 regulates granting of patents; Minister may issue patents up to ten years upon delivery of a full specification and in case of a machine full drawings and, if required, a complete model. Where the invention is a composition of matter, specimens sufficient for experiment must be furnished. The law also gives the inventor power to file a caveat, which is kept secret and gives priority for one year. If upon examination by the Commissioner of Patents he considers that claimant is justly entitled and invention sufficiently useful and important, the Minister will issue the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines formal disclosure (specification/drawings/models/specimens), substantive Commissioner examination for utility/importance, and a caveat system granting one-year priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hawaii — Foreign-patent dependency, importation and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Where foreign patents are in existence, patents may be obtained unless the thing patented has been introduced into public use in the Hawaiian Islands for more than one year prior to the application. The patent expires on the expiration of the earliest prior foreign patent. Goods made according to the invention abroad can be imported without invalidating the patent. The fees payable for application, commissioner's report, and the sealing amount to 30 dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic grant subject to local public-use bar and dependency on prior foreign patent terms; importation tolerated; fixed fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holland — No patents
rubrics_metrics.description: No patents are granted for Holland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictionally, patent protection not available (at least per this manual's statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Honduras — Absence of special law and case-by-case terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The republic has not passed any special law relative to the protection of inventions, but patents are granted for terms fixed in each case; terms similar to other Central American Republics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad hoc grant practice with terms determined case-by-case; no uniform statutory scheme described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italy — Eligible applicants and five categories of patentable subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor only, whether a native or a foreigner, or his assign, can obtain a patent of invention. Inventions are considered patentable which have for their immediate object: (1) an industrial product or result; (2) any instrument, machine, etc., or mechanical arrangement; (3) any process or method of industrial production; (4) a motor, or the industrial application of a force already known; (5) the technical application of a scientific principle in such a condition that it will produce direct industrial results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the categories of eligible inventions and restricts entitlement to the inventor or lawful assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italy — Novelty and foreign-patent/ importation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be novel. A new invention or industrial discovery patented abroad and not yet imported into Italy, although already published by means of such foreign patent, confers the right to the inventor or his assign of obtaining a patent in Italy, provided the application be made before the expiration of the foreign patent and before the importation or use of the invention by another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is required; foreign patents can confer entitlement provided national application precedes expiration and import/use by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italy — Effectivity date and certificates of addition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent of invention takes effect from the date of the application, and its duration from the last day of that one of the months of March, June, September, and December which follows next after the date of the application. Certificates of addition are granted and are annexed to the principal patent. Applications for certificates of addition made during the first six months by the owner of a patent have preference over applications for new patents made for the same invention by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines formal effectivity dating conventions and provides a six-month preference for certificates of addition (follow-on improvements).
